name: COMOROS
lead: Comoros is a small group of islands in the Indian Ocean, between Madagascar and Africa. Its name means "Islands of the Moon" in Arabic. Each of its three main islands has a volcano. Ylang-ylang flowers scent the air.

facts.label: Capital
facts.sub: Built at foot of an active volcano

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Comoros was born of fire. All three islands are volcanic. Grande Comore has Mount Karthala, an active volcano. Its crater is over 3 km wide. A small town could fit inside.
Coral reefs ring the islands. Warm rain feeds thick rainforest. Mohéli, the smallest island, is the wildest. Forest grows down to the beach, where sea turtles nest.
animals: The coelacanth is a fish people thought was extinct for 65 million years. A live one was found in 1938. It hides in deep caves off Grande Comore and grows 2 metres long.
Livingstone's fruit bat lives only in Comoros. Fewer than 1,500 remain. Its wings stretch 1.4 metres. Each island also has its own tiny scops owl, found nowhere else on Earth.
culture: The Grand Mariage is the biggest event in a Comorian life. This wedding party lasts two weeks, with feasts, dances and sultan-style costumes. Families save for years.
Music called twarab mixes the Arabic lute, the violin and Swahili poetry. For celebrations, women paint their faces with golden sandalwood paste called msindzano.
history: Arab traders brought Islam around the 10th century. They named the islands Juzur al-Qamar, or Islands of the Moon. Rival sultans ruled each island and traded spices across the sea.
France took control in the 1800s. Independence came in 1975. Then came more than 20 coups in 50 years. People called them 'the coup-coup islands'. Things are calmer now.
wows: Comoros supplies about 80% of the world's ylang-ylang oil.
Karthala erupts about every 11 years, most recently in 2007.
Comoros has had over 20 coups since 1975.
A live coelacanth was caught here in 1938.
Moroni is built on an active volcano's lava field.
Livingstone's fruit bat lives nowhere else on Earth.
In 2001, Mohéli opened sub-Saharan Africa's first community marine park.

myths.fact: No. They are two countries about 300 km apart, each with its own president.
Vanilla is a climbing orchid. Farmers pollinate each flower by hand. Comoros grows it.
